title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Vulnerabilities, Including Exploited Windows Zero-Day
key_facts: Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed a record 1,413 CVEs, including 1,102 in Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in developer tools and 36 in SharePoint Server.
This month alone exceeds all of 2025; more than 4,000 flaws fixed so far in 2026, a surge SecurityWeek says is largely driven by AI.
One Windows zero-day, CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS 8.8), is exploited in the wild: a shell flaw that bypasses Mark of the Web warnings.
Reported independently by researchers at Fujitsu, Anthropic and an independent expert.
CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list and told federal agencies to fix it by 16 Oct.
Two flaws were public before patches; Microsoft introduced 'risk cohorts' to help prioritise updates.
quote_evidence: Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix a record-breaking number of vulnerabilities, including a Windows zero-day exploited in the wild.
This month alone, Microsoft patched more vulnerabilities than it did in all of 2025.
why_it_matters_hint: Everyone running Windows needs to install this update, and the volume shows AI is speeding up bug discovery.
notes: Patch Tuesday was 13 Oct 2026; reported 14 Oct. AI as the cause of the surge is SecurityWeek's description; no figure is given.
